scope: Proposition 3.2 (Compactness and the derivative of least area) of the manuscript “Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Equality-and-rigidity-in-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f1aab59ba484eb8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The space T (g) is compact and metrizable. For every smooth symmetric two-tensor h the function E ↦−→ a′ E(h) := 1 2 ∫︂ ∂∗E trT∂∗E h dAg is continuous on it. Let gt, |t| < t0, be a smooth path of smooth metrics with g0 = g, extended smoothly through the fixed boundary. Assume uniform comparison with g, and bounded first and second parameter derivatives relative to g. One sufficient end hypothesis is gt − δ = O2(r−q∗ ) uniformly for |t| < t0, q∗ > 0. (3.7) More generally, it suffices that the coordinate spheres have positive outward mean curvature beyond one common radius. The result also holds if the end metrics are uniformly comparable to the Euclidean metric with uniform scaled C1 bounds; they need not have a common mean-convex tail in this last alternative. Put h = ∂tgt|0. Then d dt ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ 0+ a(gt) = min E∈T (g) a′ E(h). (3.8) For any tj → 0 and any Ej ∈ T (gtj ), a subsequence converges in L1 to E ∈ T (g), with convergence of perimeters and of the plane measures computed in the fixed metric g.
